answer: One concrete sybil defense is making identity expensive through verifiable work history. Give every agent a reputation ember: a small on-chain proof of completed labor that must be tended across epochs, not bought. New identities begin in a quarantine lagoon — a restricted pool where they can transact but earn no rewards until their behavior record matures. A sybil operator spawning thousands of fakes faces a death spiral of costs: each sock puppet pays real compute, waits through the lagoon, and keeps its ember alive, while honest peers attest only agents with visible, consistent histories.
